newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products mixed, gas oil soft.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products mixed, gas oil soft.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were mixed on Tuesday, traders said.
Gasoline was quiet and the market was balanced.

Demand was seen for around 20,000 tonnes of 98 RON, 0.25 percent lead gasoline containing for Lebanon. Earlier demand from Lebanon was thought to have evaporated and one dealer said she thought this requirement had been covered from Syria.
Naphtha markets remained thin. Although Algerian, Moroccan, Greek and Indian cargoes were thought to be in the market, most of those appeared to have been already committed.
An Alexandria cargo was still thought to be available.
Traders said the expected arrival of north American low sulphur gas oil in the region had cooled premiums off slightly.

"The Med was looking fairly tight 10 days ago. We sold a couple of cargoes at (Oct IPE) +$20 but the arb from north America has taken the top off the market," one trader said. "The low sulphur situation is now looking fairly balanced although there's still a little bit more demand than supply," another trader said.
A Russian cargo was heard offered at cif high +$2 cif Genoa.

A Tunisian tender to buy up to 200,000 tonnes of high sulphur cracked fuel oil for delivery between now and January has been delayed. The tender was to have been awarded on Tuesday, but higher bids were required. The announcement will be officially made on Friday. Some traders thought prices would be around mean fob Med +$11.50-12.00 cif Tunisia.
High sulphur fuel remains tight with prices steady around $104-107 fob Med. Bunker quality continues to be scarce.
Low sulphur cracked cargoes were also firm around $124-126 cif Med, amid tight supplies and continued bullish talk of a trader with a short into Turkey. -- London newsroom +44 171 542 8167
